Trees up to c. 40 feet tall with a measured trunk diameter of 12-13 inches maximum. As one proceeds to the Woronora River others are seen quite commonly but scattered and mostly in the vicinity of 20 feet tall or a little less. None was observed with the usual somewhat 'mallee-like' habit of A. obtusifolia on the higher Blue Mountains. Compared to material in my herbarium the phyllodes are on the whole narrower, much longer, and with longer petioles than those from the higher Blue Mountains. In addition the longitudinal venation seems less distinct but this may be due to comparing dry to half-dry material. The habit of the tree or shrub is, of course, much more robust and tall at Engadine - Heathcote. No pods were available but a further, more exacting search will be made.
